stage_b_reviewed_content.statement:
Convention: a ring is commutative with $1$; an $R$-algebra is associative, unital and central over $R$.

Let $R$ be a ring. Let $(A, \text{d})$ and $(B, \text{d})$ be
differential graded algebras over $R$. Let $M$ be a right differential
graded $B$-module. There is a $1$-to-$1$ correspondence
between $(A, B)$-bimodule structures on $M$ compatible with the given
differential graded $B$-module structure and homomorphisms
$$
A
\longrightarrow
\Hom_{\text{Mod}^{dg}_{(B, \text{d})}}(M, M)
$$
of differential graded $R$-algebras.

graded $B$-module.
conclusions:
There is a $1$-to-$1$ correspondence
between $(A, B)$-bimodule structures on $M$ compatible with the given
differential graded $B$-module structure and homomorphisms
$$
A
\longrightarrow
\Hom_{\text{Mod}^{dg}_{(B, \text{d})}}(M, M)
$$
of differential graded $R$-algebras.

reason: The earlier left-action/endomorphism-algebra correspondence identifies a compatible left A-action on right B-module M with a dg algebra map A→End_R(M). Compatibility with right B-action means precisely that each image endomorphism is B-linear, so the homomorphism factors through the dg B-linear endomorphism subalgebra; only the routine compatibility calculation is omitted.

stage_b_reviewed_content.statement:
Convention: a ring is commutative with $1$; an $R$-algebra is associative, unital and central over $R$.

For a differential graded $(A,B)$-bimodule, property (P) means an exhaustive filtration $0=F_{-1}P\subset F_0P\subset\cdots$ by dg $(A,B)$-subbimodules with graded $(A,B)$-split inclusions and quotients direct sums of shifts $(A\otimes_R B)[k]$.

Let $R$ be a ring. Let $(A, \text{d})$ and $(B, \text{d})$ be
differential graded $R$-algebras. Let $P$ be a
differential graded $(A, B)$-bimodule having property (P)
with corresponding filtration $F_\bullet$, then we obtain a
short exact sequence
$$
0 \to
\bigoplus\nolimits F_iP \to
\bigoplus\nolimits F_iP \to P \to 0
$$
of differential graded $(A, B)$-bimodules which is split as a sequence
of graded $(A, B)$-bimodules.

reason: The signed equivalence from dg (A,B)-bimodules to right dg A^opp⊗B-modules carries the property-(P) filtration to the previously proved telescope exact sequence. Graded-splitness is preserved under the equivalence, giving the asserted short exact sequence.
